hypotheses.name: Month-end pension rebalancing pressure on US equity-index CFDs (Harvey-Mazzoleni-Melone Calendar x week-4 signal), equity-only, server-day holds
hypotheses.mechanism: Balanced (60/40-type) institutional portfolios rebalance on a calendar schedule, mostly at month-end. Mature pension funds also sell assets before month-end to pay member benefits (Etula et al. 2020, cited by the paper). Overlay managers execute the rebalance with S&P 500 and Treasury futures. When stocks have beaten bonds month-to-date, rebalancers must sell equities in the last days of the month. That predictable, price-insensitive flow depresses next-day equity returns, and the pressure reverses within about two weeks. The paper finds no predictive power for the Calendar signal outside month-end, and none in a value-vs-growth falsification test.
hypotheses.rule: PRE-REGISTERABLE, ZERO FREE PARAMETERS BEYOND THE PAPER. Calendar: T(m) = last NYSE business day of month m (NYSE holiday calendar, known in advance). Equity leg R_E(t) = US500 CFD return from the last server-day close (16:55 ET) of T(m-1) to the server-day close of day t (FTMO 1D bars). Bond leg R_B(t) = 10y Treasury month-to-date return through day t-1 only: -8.5 x (DGS10(t-1) - DGS10(T(m-1))) / 100, with FRED DGS10 lagged one business day for H.15 publication. Robustness variant: equity-only. Signal S(t) = 0.6(1+R_E)/(0.6(1+R_E)+0.4(1+R_B)) - 0.6, computed after the 16:55 ET close of day t. For every t in the last five NYSE business days of the month {T-4..T}: hold -sign(S(t)) on the NEXT server day. Entry at the first bar after the 17:00-18:00 ET break; exit at the last bar before 16:55 ET. No swap, no weekend hold. The return days are therefore T-3, T-2, T-1, T, T+1. Primary family (BH q=0.10): US500, US30, USTEC, all using the same US500/DGS10 signal. Secondary family, paper Sec. 3.5: DE40, FRA40, AUS200 with S(t) applied to server day t+2 (one-day lag, as in the paper). Pre-declared descriptive subset: return days T-3..T-1 only, because they do not overlap the days G7 read. Measurement as in the repo: net of the FTMO hourly relative spread at the entry/exit hours (median and p90), CR1 SE by date. Calendar null: (a) net > 0, and (b) excess over the same -sign(S) rule applied on all non-week-4 server days with the same weekday (the paper's beta2 interaction) > 0. Execution: risk 1% of the account at the stop. Stop = 2.0 x trailing-20-server-day SD of open-to-close returns (PIT). Size = 1% / stop distance. Exit at the server-day close if the stop is not hit.
hypotheses.holding: One server day per trade (about 18:00 ET to 16:55 ET). Five consecutive trade days per month. Flat before every 17:00 ET rollover, so no swap and no weekend exposure (meets FTMO funded-Standard weekend rule).
hypotheses.expected_effect: PUBLISHED (NBER w33554, daily S&P 500 and 10y T-note futures, 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17): a one-SD rise in the Calendar signal lowers next-day equity returns by about 17 bp and raises bond returns by about 2 bp. This is a partial coefficient, controlling for momentum (Table 1 t-stats around 4). The S&P-vs-T-note front-running strategy has Sharpe 1.11 gross, about 1 net, and 0.90 excluding Sep-2008 to Mar-2009 and Mar-2020. It returns 15.7-18.0% p.a. in high-friction regimes vs 3.8-5.1% in low ones. NOT REPORTED: the raw, equity-only, sign-only effect on a single index. That is the object traded here, so its size is UNKNOWN. My prior is 5-15 bp per trade day before costs, with the momentum offset as the main downside. IN-REPO POWER (unconditional server-day open-to-close SD only; no outcome read): US500 SD 114 bp/day; 105 months x 5 = 525 return days 2018-01 to 2026-09; MDE (80% power, one-sided 5%) 12.4 bp on the full span, 16.0 bp on a 60% split. US30 SD 114 bp, 450 days, MDE 13.4 / 17.3 bp. USTEC SD 145 bp, MDE 15.8 bp. Under the repo's exact 3-read split (development < 2024-03), US500 discovery has about 222 days (MDE about 19 bp), confirmation about 148 (about 23 bp), exposed about 155 (about 23 bp). The joint pass probability at a true 10-15 bp effect is low (rough estimate under 20%).

citations.title: Harvey, Mazzoleni, Melone (2025, rev. Jan 2026), The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing, NBER WP 33554
citations.what_it_supports: Mechanism. Calendar/Threshold signal construction (App. B, eqs B.1-B.2). The 17 bp next-day equity effect per 1-SD signal. Predictability concentrated in the last 4-5 days of the month (Fig. 3, week4 interaction). Positive coefficients in weeks 1 and 3 (reversal, fn 27). Effect insignificant in 1961-1997 and significant in 1997-2023. Similar coefficients for international indices with signals lagged one day (Sec. 3.5, Table D.14). Strategy Sharpe 1.11, 0.90 ex-crises, concentrated in high-VIX regimes (Table 6). Authors' claim (fn 32): extending the sample through 2025 makes the results stronger (not shown).

hypotheses.data_needed_and_pit: IN REPO: FTMO 1D bars for US500/USTEC/DE40/FRA40 from 2017-12 and US30/AUS200 from 2019-02 (data/history/ftmo/ohlcv.*.1D). The edge families read only dense-5m days (US500/USTEC/DE40/FRA40 from 2021-09; US30 from 2019-02). So the 2018-01 to 2021-08 daily outcomes look unread by any edge family I found. Older Wyckoff/ICT stability backtests span 2018+; confirm in the research ledger before calling that window clean. Hourly spreads come from data/history/costs/ftmo/symbolspec.*.json. NOT IN REPO: (1) a 10y Treasury series. FRED DGS10 (H.15) is published with about a one-business-day lag, so the bond leg must be lagged one day for PIT; CME 10y note settlements are an alternative if a PIT daily source exists. (2) The NYSE holiday calendar, which is static and known in advance (PIT-safe). The signal uses only the closes of days <= t and bond data <= t-1. The trade starts after the 18:00 ET reopen, so availableTime <= decisionTime holds. Server-day/DST mapping should follow the repo's mt5_bridge server timezone (server midnight = 17:00 ET).
hypotheses.cost_sensitivity: Low. One round trip per server day. Median relative spread at the entry (18:00 ET) and exit (around 16:55 ET) hours is about 0.6-0.9 bp on US500 (40-50 points at about 6,500), about 0.4-0.6 bp on US30 and about 0.6-0.8 bp on USTEC. That is under 10% of a 10 bp gross effect, and 2x-spread stress is still under 2 bp. Swap is avoided by exiting before the rollover. Holding a short through the rollover would earn about +0.13 bp; a long would pay about -3.15 bp/night (docs/audits/2026-10-03-ftmo-rules-audit.md section 2). DE40/FRA40 outside the cash session cost more (up to 125-160 points); the secondary family must use the hourly spread at its actual entry/exit hours.
hypotheses.frequency_per_year: 12 monthly episodes x 5 server-day trades = about 60 trades per instrument per year (about 180 across US500/US30/USTEC, but these are about 0.9 correlated, so effectively about 60 independent trade days and 12 clustered episodes).
hypotheses.expected_corr_with_gold_intraday_trend: Expected about 0. The driver is stock-bond rebalancing flows, unrelated to intraday gold trend continuation (H7/G9). UNMEASURED. Risk: the published payoff is concentrated in high-volatility/crisis months, when the gold trend book also tends to earn, so tail co-movement may be positive. Measure with book_sim.py compare against docs/architecture/book-baseline.json before claiming a diversification benefit.
hypotheses.snooping_or_contamination_risk: MODERATE, disclosed. (1) G7 (unconditional long on the last trading day and the first 3 days of each month; all three reads; positive non-significant nets on US500/US30/USTEC) read 2 of the 5 return days (T and T+1). Following the published rule unchanged, rather than cutting those days because G7 is known, avoids selection by me. The known positive G7 nets work against a mostly-short rule, so including them is conservative. The T-3..T-1 subset is reported descriptively only. (2) H1 (20-day momentum sign to next server day, all days, three reads) used a predictor highly correlated with the month-to-date signal in week 4. Its pooled result (null in discovery, momentum won in confirmation) partly informs this test. The week-4 interaction itself was never read. (3) The Threshold (any-day) signal is NOT proposed: it is too close to H1 and needs the momentum control the paper uses. (4) The hypothesis comes from a 2025 publication, not from repo data. (5) Post-publication crowding: wide 2025 press coverage plus sell-side pension-rebalancing estimates (pre-dating the paper) could pull the flow earlier (T-6..T-4). That would show as decay, not as a false positive.
hypotheses.source_sample_and_decay: Source sample: daily futures 1997-09-10 to 2023-03-17 (main), plus 1961-2023 using index data. Coefficients are indistinguishable from zero in 1961-1997 and significant in 1997-2023, so the effect depends on the size of the institutional rebalancing regime. Authors' footnote 32 says that extending through 2025 makes the results 'even stronger' (claim only, numbers not shown). There is no independent post-publication test that I could find or open. The repo's unread FTMO daily window 2018-01 to 2021-08 (to be confirmed) overlaps the paper's sample, so it is a replication on a different instrument (CFD), not out-of-sample for the paper. True post-paper data: 2023-03-18 onward, about 3.5 years, about 210 return days, MDE about 20 bp. Not enough on its own.

KILLED CLASSES (reason; source opened unless marked):
1. Pre-FOMC drift (Lucca-Moench; S&P 500 +49 bp in the 2pm-2pm window, 1994-2011; also in international indices), including a swap-free overnight version (18:00 to 09:30 ET before the FOMC day). Killed on documented decay: 'essentially disappeared after 2015' (Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert, FRL 2021, sample to Dec-2019). The Fed's Knox and Vissing-Jorgensen (FEDS 2026-023) report about 20 bp/meeting overnight drift on average Apr-2011 to Dec-2023, but that average spans the pre-2016 years, so it does not show a revival. Power: about 60 FOMC nights on US30, overnight SD 66 bp, MDE about 21 bp (27 bp in discovery). Value: about 8 trades/yr. NEAREST MISS: forward-only if anything. URLs: https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr512.html, https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/finlet/v40y2021ics1544612320315956.html, https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/files/2026023pap.pdf
2. Macro-announcement-day premium (Savor-Wilson; Ai-Bansal-Guo NBER w31923): 10.68 bp on about 44 days/yr (t 5.36), 1961-2023. FOMC days 17.61 bp; non-FOMC days 8.65 bp. 16.33 bp in Jan-2020 to Aug-2023. Well documented and not decayed, but UNVALIDATABLE here. Daily SD is 114 bp. ISM (always business day 1) and some NFP days fall inside G7's read window and must be excluded. That leaves about 26/yr and an MDE of about 19 bp on US500 versus a non-FOMC effect of about 9 bp; 80% power would need about 45 years. No opened source fixes an intraday window that would cut variance, so choosing one now would be snooping. It also needs a historical release calendar, which is not in the repo. URL: https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w31923/w31923.pdf
3. FOMC-cycle even weeks (Cieslak-Morse-Vissing-Jorgensen 2019). Killed: the cycle flipped to a statistically significant opposite sign in 2017-2021 (Knox and Vissing-Jorgensen, FEDS 2026-023, section 6.2), so there is no ex-ante sign.
4. Market intraday momentum / gamma and LETF hedging (Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens, JFE 2021: rest-of-day return predicts the last 30 min, 60+ futures, 1974-2020). Killed as contaminated and already tested. E7 (Gao: first half-hour predicts the last 30 min) read the same outcome window on all 6 index CFDs over the development data: not significant in discovery (p 0.057, sign '-'), net -1.0 bp in confirmation. The conditional negative-gamma version needs options gamma data, which is not in the repo. URL: https://repub.eur.nl/pub/131621
5. MOC/closing-auction imbalance (last 10-30 min) on US indices. Killed on data: NYSE/Nasdaq imbalance feeds are not in the repo. The 'close overshoot then overnight reversal' LETF-predation channel is documented for Korean single stocks in 2026, and the same paper notes that US index LETF rebalancing has 'modest price impact' (Ivanov-Lenkey 2018 et al., not opened). F6 already found overnight CONTINUATION after US-session sell-offs on these CFDs. URL: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.03703
6. Index futures expiry, quad witching and index-rebalance days. Killed on power: 4/yr gives about 35 events on US500 and an MDE of about 48 bp/day. Literature says expiry effects moved to the open and diminished after the 1987 settlement change (UNVERIFIED: search snippets only; Stoll-Whaley not opened). Index-level direction on rebalance days has no source.
7. Option-expiration week (Stivers-Sun JBF 2013; 1988-2010; S&P 100 OE-week average 0.528%/week per Quantpedia). Killed: the main claim is relative (S&P 100 vs equal-weighted) and the allowlist has no small-cap leg. Absolute weekly MDE on US500 is about 62 bp from 105 weeks. Dilution by weekly/daily expiries is my inference (unverified). URLs: https://quantpedia.com/strategies/option-expiration-week-effect, https://www.cxoadvisory.com/calendar-effects/option-expiration-week-stock-return-drill-down/
8. Gold around the LBMA AM/PM auctions after the 2015 reform. Killed on documented decay: Aspris-Foley-Gratton-O'Neill (EFMA 2017) show reduced adjusted returns, volatility and return predictability in the futures after the electronic auctions. Pre-2015 fix drift (Caminschi-Heaney 2014, Abrantes-Metz: unverified, not opened) is tied to a mechanism that no longer exists. URL: https://efmaefm.org/0EFMAMEETINGS/EFMA%20ANNUAL%20MEETINGS/2017-Athens/papers/EFMA2017_0580_fullpaper.pdf
9. Gold around COMEX settlement (13:30 ET). Killed: no documented directional mechanism found.
10. Gold vs real yields/USD at US release times. Killed: no PIT yield/DXY intraday data and no historical calendar in the repo. It would also be a continuation signal that loads on the H7/G9 trend factor.
11. Gold time-of-day (Asia-hours drift). Killed: still no cited directional window (B8 stays blocked). The Tokyo/NY gold-futures seasonality paper found (Iwatsubo-Watkins-Xu 2018) is about efficiency, liquidity and volume, not direction (search result only).
12. DE40 Xetra closing auction. Killed: no documented index-level directional effect found.
13. ECB/RBA announcement days for DE40/FRA40/AUS200. Killed: Brusa-Savor-Wilson find no premium for non-Fed central banks (quoted in Ai-Bansal-Guo, opened). FOMC spillover is covered by item 1.
14. Unconditional overnight drift of US index futures (Boyarchenko-Larsen-Whelan). Killed: the paper's own unconditional window is negative net of spread (repo record, reframes R6a), and F6 read the unconditional nights as its placebo.
15. Turn-of-month / pre-holiday. Turn-of-month is contaminated (G7, three reads). Pre-holiday: no opened source and about 9/yr (MDE about 32 bp).
16. Harvey Threshold (any-day) component. Killed: its equity-only form is close to H1 (20-day momentum sign), which was read in all three windows (null; momentum won in confirmation).

fatal_issues: Cost: the source's own gross (33%/yr ~= 0.078%/trade; excess over BTC drift ~0.065-0.072%) is below the 0.10% taker round trip, so the expected net at the repo's primary cost is negative before any test. The rule's own kill criterion fires by arithmetic.

The maker scenario cannot be judged: a fill at the touch at a fixed clock time cannot be modeled from klines (the repo's R6(f)/R2 limit-fill problem). Even assuming the full source premium and 100% maker fills, net ~+0.03%/trade gives t ~0.9 in discovery and ~1.1 in confirmation. It cannot discriminate.

Most recent and most direct evidence points the other way: Schmidt & Kraft (SSRN 7384239, Bitstamp 5m 2020-2026, DST transitions as identification) report per the search-engine summary that 'hour of day predicts trading volume and volatility but not the direction of returns'. SSRN refused the connection, so this is unverified, but it is exactly the DST test XA1 proposes, already run on overlapping data.

The DST mechanism diagnostic is mis-specified. It says 'one hour after the NYSE close (20:00 UTC in DST, 21:00 UTC in standard time)', but those are the close times themselves. Under either reading, the close-anchored window equals the fixed 21:00 UTC window in one of the two DST regimes, so only one regime discriminates. The A-minus-B difference of the overlapping windows has SD ~1.6% (sqrt(2) x hourly 1.15%), which gives t < 1 for a one-hour premium shift. It cannot falsify the mechanism.

Contamination: discovery 2020-01 to 2022-12 lies entirely inside the source sample (Gemini to 2022-02) and Quantpedia's public update (to 2023-06). BTC venues are arbitraged to within basis points, so it is a replication, not a discovery read. Only 2023-07+ is blind, and the hypothesis puts it in CONFIRMATION/EXPOSED.

fatal_issues: The event count is overstated. The 104-weekend PIT lookback on BTCUSDT perp data starting 2020-01 makes the first eligible weekend 2021-12-31. Measured events: 2022: 8, 2023: 5, 2024: 12, 2025: 12, 2026 to Sep: 5, so 42 in total, not 60-70. US500 dense 5m data also starts only 2021-09-15 (first complete 16:00 to 09:30 observation in the repo data). With three reads that is ~10-15 events per read.

Power is near zero. The US500 unconditional daily SD is 1.18% (repo 1D), and risk-off Mondays are higher. A ~15-event read has SE ~0.35-0.45% and MDE ~0.8-0.9%. The tradable target is the post-reopen RESIDUAL, which no source measures and which should be a small fraction of the move: the Yahoo/Binance Research article reports weekend on-chain prices capturing a median 92% of Monday's gap.

The evidence is unstable in sign. The practitioner source shows ES opening -0.48% after BTC drops in 2024-26, but +0.77% after drops (and -0.81% after surges) over 2021-26. That is the opposite sign and larger than the recent effect. The FRL paper's windows, sample and coefficients are not visible.

The stop at 1.5 x ATR(1h,24) on US500 (~0.5%) binds against a ~1.2% SD over 21 hours. By a reflection-principle estimate (my arithmetic) about 2/3 of trades would stop out, so the primary statistic would mostly measure stop mechanics.
No read periods are specified in the hypothesis.
required_design_changes: If revived: state the read periods and the true event count (~42) with an MDE per read. Use the Binance spot archive (2017-08+) only to feed the lookback (signal side), and say that US500 venue data caps the sample at 2021-09+.
Make the time exit primary. Any stop should be >= 4-5 sigma of the window return.

Accept in advance that a null result here will be 'underpowered', not 'dead' (reframes R6(b)). Given that, it is not worth spending the family budget now. A forward-only pre-registration is the honest alternative.
verdicts.citation_check: Opened: (1) RePEc FRL 86 (Mourey, Shahrour, Soiman) abstract: confirms 20 cryptos (~85% of market cap), Bayesian/Kalman, negative weekend returns predict Monday equity declines while positive ones do not, robust across Nasdaq/R2000/S&P sectors, strengthened after LUNA. No sample, return window or effect size. The HAL version (hal-05415054) returned 403. (2) TradingView ClashChartsTeam: ~100 weekends over 2 years, +/-1.5% buckets, gaps -0.48/+0.03/+0.18%, claims '99.9%' significance on ~100 weekends. The 5-year (2021-2026) results flip to +0.77% (drop) and -0.81% (surge). Monday follow-through is NOT studied. MATCHES the hypothesis's description and is more damaging than stated. (3) Yahoo/Insider Monkey: median 92% of Monday's gap priced by weekend tokenized-equity trading, Binance Research data to 2026-07-28 (~one quarter); post-open behavior not addressed. MATCHES.
verdicts.power_estimate: Measured events: 42 (2022-01 to 2026-09). About 10-15 per read under a three-read split. SE ~0.35-0.45% and MDE ~0.8-0.9% on US500, versus an unknown residual that is plausibly < 0.2%. Power < 10%.

fatal_issues: The citations do not support the rule as specified. Kurihara & Matsumoto uses SPOT 1m closes for illiquid coins (BIFI, CITY, GNO, PIVX, QKC) in four ~1-month windows, a LightGBM classifier (not a threshold rule), a fee of 0.02% per trade (below the 0.05% perp taker), and buy-and-hold as the benchmark (not a zero/placebo null). It also reports lag-0 and lag-1 correlations as 'comparable'. The Guo et al. abstract gives no frequency, horizon or magnitude (the 2.16%/day figure is unverified). Jia et al. report the OPPOSITE (negative) intraday sign. The net prior for a positive, after-cost, 2-second-latency catch-up on liquid perps is about 0, with unknown sign.

The cost hurdle is structurally binding: taker 0.10% round trip plus alt spread and slippage is ~0.12-0.15%, against a minimum qualifying gap of 0.10%. The trade only pays if the catch-up after the 2s haircut exceeds 100% of the measured gap on the smaller events.

Lag-1 correlation in 1m-close data is plausibly a stale-last-print (non-synchronous trading) artifact in thinner alts. This is general microstructure knowledge, not verified here. The gap g_i measured from 1m closes overstates the exploitable gap. The 2s aggTrade entry prices this correctly, which is why the expected net is about minus the cost.

It cannot be validated for deployment. The venue is TESTNET, whose fills do not reflect mainnet microstructure, and the latency of the repo's REST path is unmeasured. A 5-minute chase strategy's live edge depends on sub-second execution, so even a positive backtest would not be a validated method.

The data and funding assumptions are wrong or thin. The current fapi/v1/fundingInfo (verified 2026-10-03) shows ONDO, TAO, RENDER, VIRTUAL and ASTER on 4h funding intervals; SUI, BTC, ETH and SOL are on 8h. So the '00/08/16 UTC' exclusion is wrong for 5 of 6 test alts. fundingInfo is also current-only (not PIT), so historical stamps must come from the fundingRate archive. ASTER aggTrades start 2025-09 and SUI 2023-05 (verified in the S3 listing), which leaves thin per-coin reads. 1m alt klines and aggTrades are not in the repo.
required_design_changes: If revived: start with a cheap falsification on 1m data alone. Is the catch-up measured from the first aggTrade >= 2s after bar close still larger than 0.15% on average for gaps >= 0.10%? Stop if not.
Take funding stamps from the per-symbol fundingRate archive (4h for most of these alts), not from a fixed 00/08/16 grid.
Include spread and slippage estimated from aggTrades at the entry second. Report the sign two-sided as planned, and make the ETH/SOL controls a pre-registered pass condition (no lag in controls).
Do not plan live use until the latency of the mainnet execution path is measured. Testnet results are not evidence.

(2) SMU repository (Guo, Sang, Tu, Wang) abstract: Binance data, lagged cross-coin returns predict, adaptive LASSO/PCA, 'sizable' out-of-sample long-short returns after costs; no frequency, horizon or magnitude. verdicts.power_estimate: Event count not measured (1m alt data not imported). Likely hundreds to thousands of alt-events per year, heavily clustered by event minute and regime. Effective N is limited by clustering and by the short histories (ASTER ~13 months, VIRTUAL ~22, RENDER ~27). The binding constraint is the cost hurdle (~0.12-0.15%) against a plausible catch-up, not N.

fatal_issues: Underpowered. With US500 dense 5m data starting 2021-09-15 and a 60-day lookback, measured 2-sigma overnight shocks (09:30 ET open vs prior 15:55-bar close) are 2021: 1, 2022: 21, 2023: 7, 2024: 15, 2025: 23, 2026 to Sep: 13. With BTC co-movement there are 71 events in total. BTC's 6.4h SD is 1.2-2.3% unconditionally and higher on shock days (~2-2.5%, my assumption). A read of ~15-30 events has MDE ~0.9-1.3%.

The co-movement filter is nearly non-binding: about 89% (71/80) of shocks pass. This uses my approximation of BTC's price at 09:30 ET from the 1h bar (signal side only), so it does not isolate an 'overreaction leg'.

The rule has no source support. The Jia, Shen & Zhang abstract does not define 'large price swings', the sample, the frequency or the reversal horizon. The reversal it documents could be completed during the overnight window itself, before the 09:35 ET entry. The Science of Money summary covers contemporaneous co-movement only (hourly BTC against DAILY index data) and explicitly reports no predictability or reversal. The rule is the author's own construction on a 2024 paywalled abstract.
The stop at 2.5 x ATR(1h,24) (~1.5%) binds on shock days, where the window SD is ~2%. A reflection estimate (my arithmetic) gives ~30-45% stop-outs, which changes the statistic.
No read periods are specified. The event days are macro-shock days on which the gold book is most active, so independence is unmeasured exactly where it matters.
required_design_changes: If revived: obtain the paper's actual shock definition and reversal horizon before building, and drop the co-movement filter or justify it. As written, it removes ~11% of events with no stated rationale.
Pre-register reads, the per-read event count (~71 in total) and the MDE. Make the time exit primary.
Report the daily-P&L correlation with the H7+G9 gold book on event days only.
verdicts.citation_check: Opened: (1) RePEc IREF 90 (Jia, Shen, Zhang) abstract: high-frequency BTC data, intraday BTC reversals after large stock-market price swings (overreaction), stronger and more persistent for developed markets, determinants are network effect, sentiment, EPU and attention. No sample, swing definition, horizon or effect size. PARTLY supports the hypothesis (direction of the effect only). (2) Science of Money (Zhang, Peng, Ma, John): April 2013 to January 2023; hourly BTC with DAILY index data; 1% index move ~ 0.30% BTC; S&P 500 dominant in its trading hours and TSX overnight; contemporaneous co-movement only, explicitly not causal, no reversal. Supports only the co-movement leg.

MDE ~0.9-1.3% per event, against an unknown source magnitude. Power < 10%. These signal-side counts and unconditional vol/funding stats must be disclosed as prior reads in any pre-registration.

fatal_issues: The platform cannot execute it. The repo trades only Binance USDT-M futures testnet, with no spot account, and the long-spot leg is the whole trade. Opening a spot or portfolio-margin account is a new venue and API-key surface, which makes it a trust-boundary change and an owner decision. Until that decision is made, even a positive read is not a usable method.

No clean discovery sample. HMRV's sample is 2020-01-08 to 2024-03-11 (Table 2) and sits entirely inside the proposed dev window (2020-01 to 2025-03), so discovery and confirmation would replicate a published result rather than test it. The only clean data starts 2024-03-12. HMRV's own Table 8 shows the BTC price-convergence component had already fallen to 3.30%/yr at zero cost in 2024 Q1 (zero-cost BTC return 21.44%/yr that year).

The cost threshold makes events vanishingly rare after 2022. With c = 0.30% and r = 5%, rho = 1095*prem + 0.4975, so entry needs prem > 0.255%, i.e. rho > 3.285. HMRV Table 4 gives post-2022 BTC rho mean 0.17 and sd 0.42 (annualised), which puts our entry about 7.4 sd above the mean (HMRV's own High tier is about 3.9 sd). In the clean window the event count per symbol-year is plausibly in single digits, which cannot discriminate.

By construction the rule earns about the cost on the price leg. Opening at rho = kappa*c and closing at rho = 0 captures a premium change of roughly c, which is the round-trip cost. Any net edge must come from overshoot past the threshold plus funding received, so the trade is effectively DF-2 (funding capture) with an entry trigger. The cited decomposition (37.61 of 52.55 %/yr from price convergence) is for the ZERO-cost, always-active strategy (Tables 6 and 8), not for any tradeable fee tier.

The cost benchmark is mis-anchored. HMRV's 'High' tier is MAKER fees for a trader doing more than $1M spot and more than $15M perp volume per 30 days (Table 3 and the Section 4 text), not a VIP0 retail taker. The gap to our cost is therefore larger than the 1.8x stated, and no published result exists at our cost.
required_design_changes: (For any resubmission.) Get an owner decision on spot-leg execution first, routed as a trust-boundary change. Otherwise re-specify the trade as a new, futures-only hypothesis (perp vs USDT-M quarterly delivery calendar basis), with its own pre-registration.
Start discovery after 2024-03-11. Label 2020-01 to 2024-03 as replication-only and exclude it from BH and from the decision.

Before reading any P&L, pre-register an event-count gate: count rho > kappa*c entries (signal only, no returns) in the clean window, and declare the family untestable if pooled events are below a pre-stated N (for example 30).

Cost: taker fees on both legs (spot 0.10%, or 0.075% with BNB; perp 0.05%), plus half the effective spread per leg, plus funding booked by calc_time. Mark both legs to market hourly and report return on total capital (spot plus perp margin), not on notional.
Sizing: set the 1%-of-account loss at a basis-blowout stop that includes the perp-leg liquidation buffer. Notional will be a multiple of the account, so state it.
Nulls: always-on carry (HMRV Table 7 'Carry') and random entry with matched holding time. The tradeable claim is mean net P&L per round trip > 0 with CR1-by-date SE.

verdicts.power_estimate: Effectively zero in the clean window. Entry is about 7.4 sd above the post-2022 mean rho at c = 0.30%, so expect single-digit events per symbol-year after 2024-03. The full-sample HMRV High-tier rate (about 20/yr BTC, 27/yr ETH) is dominated by 2020-2021.

fatal_issues: Same spot-leg execution gap as DF-1. The platform has no spot account, so the long-spot leg cannot be traded without a new venue and API-key integration (a trust-boundary change and an owner decision).

The test statistic is structurally biased against the filter, so it cannot isolate the filter's value. Binance funding = P + clamp(0.01% - P, -0.05%, +0.05%) (HMRV Appendix and Section 4 parameters iota = 0.01%/8h, gamma = 0.05%). In quiet markets funding is therefore pinned at +0.01%/8h (about 10.95%/yr), which always-on carry collects and the filter forgoes while it waits for FR21 >= 0.02%. 'Filtered minus always-on' is then mostly a measure of how many bear episodes had negative funding, i.e. a handful of regime episodes.

Effective N is the number of regime episodes, not entries. BTC, ETH and SOL funding regimes co-move (HMRV: deviations 'comove across currencies'), so 3 symbols x 1-5 entries/yr x about 5 years collapses to roughly 5-15 independent episodes. Clustering by entry week does not fix the dependence across regimes. The test cannot discriminate.

Evidence of decay omitted, and contamination. Christin v1.2 Epoch 5 (2022-05-09 to 2023-06-23) shows Tether-margined carry at only 1.03%/yr (SR 1.31), and Borri et al. show 2025 negative. Every carry sample overlaps the dev window, and the 2025 collapse is common knowledge, so any filter design is informed by the outcome.

Without a filter effect, the trade is a published yield (carry), not a new edge. The unconditional result is already known (positive 2020-2024, negative 2025), so a read adds little decision value for the owner.
required_design_changes: (For any resubmission.) Resolve spot-leg execution first, as an owner decision.

Replace 'excess over always-on' with a pre-registered decomposition: funding received in ON vs OFF periods, entry/exit basis P&L, and costs. Cluster SE by regime episode, pooled across symbols, and pre-state the minimum number of episodes.
Fix thresholds as multiples of Binance's iota = 0.01%/8h baseline. Read funding_interval_hours per symbol, because ASTER and others settle every 4h.
Report return on total capital (spot plus margin) and the liquidation buffer on the short-perp leg, and express the 1% rule as loss at the basis or liquidation stop.
Treat 2020-2024 as replication. Only 2025-06 onward is clean for a filter claim.

verdicts.power_estimate: Low. About 5-15 independent regime episodes over 2020-2025 across BTC/ETH/SOL. The filter-vs-always-on difference is driven by a few bear episodes, so an MDE cannot be stated meaningfully.

fatal_issues: Power is fatally low at a 7-day horizon. Unconditional non-overlapping 7-day log-return sd from repo data (data/history/binance_um, 2020-2026): BTC 8.4%, ETH 11.4%, SOL 15.8%. With 40-120 pooled events, about 25-70 in discovery and fewer effective because of cross-symbol regime overlap, the SE is about 1.5-2% and the MDE about 4-5% per 7 days. No cited source supports an effect that large at 7 days.

The evidence is at the wrong horizon or tests the wrong variable. K33 is negative 30-day-average funding over 30-360-day holds, with about 7 episodes since 2018 ('seventh time since 2018'), in-sample and overlapping. Presto finds predictive R^2 of about 0 at 7 days, though for funding CHANGES, not levels. Berachah finds the short-leg price component not significant. HMV is equity-index and FX futures at monthly horizons. Nothing supports a 7-day contrarian effect in crypto.

Member (a) is contaminated. The famous negative-funding bottoms (2020-03, 2021-06/07, 2022-11, the 2026 streak) are publicly known outcomes. Members (b) and (c) have no supporting evidence, so 3 members x 3 symbols is mostly a search over noise in a low-power regime.

Point-in-time vintage of the OI/long-short archive cannot be verified. S3 LastModified shows BTCUSDT metrics for 2020-2021 re-uploaded in 2026-03, and almost all BTC/ETH/SOL files for 2024-03 to 2026-07 (which includes the exposed window) uploaded in 2026-07/08. These are retroactive publications, not contemporaneous snapshots, and Binance's methodology at regeneration is unknown. Giagkiozis & Said found Binance BTC_USDT_P OI irreconcilable with volume over Jul 1 - Sep 30 2023.
required_design_changes: (For any resubmission.) Collapse to one pre-registered member (funding level), or one composite, to avoid a 9-cell family at low power.
Move the decision to 00:15 UTC, or use rows with create_time <= 23:50. A 00:00:05 decision does not show that the 00:00 rows were published.
Dedupe early BTC rows (verified: 576 rows/288 timestamps on 2020-09-01, identical duplicates). Handle the empty top-trader columns (verified empty all day on 2022-11-09).
Snapshot archive ETags/LastModified as a data vintage, and cross-check the archive against REST openInterestHist on the last 30 days before any read.
Pre-state the MDE and an event/episode-count gate, and abort the read if the expected MDE exceeds a plausible effect (for example 2% per week).
If the horizon is changed to 30-90 days to match K33, N falls below 15 episodes and the hypothesis is untestable. Do not do it.

verdicts.power_estimate: MDE about 4-5% per 7 days in discovery (sd 8-16% per week, N_eff of about 25-50). Plausible effects are well under 1%/week, so the test cannot discriminate.

fatal_issues: Underpowered for plausible effect sizes. Repo 1h data: about 2% of hours have |r| >= 3 sigma (trailing 720h), about 170 per symbol-year (BTC/ETH/SOL, 2020-2022 subsample). The OI <= -1.5% filter cuts that to an unknown fraction. Discovery (BTC metrics from 2020-09, ETH/SOL from 2021-12, 60% of dev) is about 6.7 symbol-years, so roughly 100-300 events but only about 60-150 date clusters, because BTC/ETH/SOL shock in the same hours. Post-shock 6h sd is about 3-4% (unconditional 6h sd is BTC 1.56%, ETH 2.05%, SOL 3.06%, and higher after shocks). The one-sample fade MDE is about 1% and the pre-registered contrast MDE about 1.5%. A plausible partial reversal is tens of bp, so the test cannot discriminate.

No direct evidence and an adverse local prior. Wen et al.'s abstract says only that intraday momentum and reversal both exist, with no number for post-jump reversal. GRX's mean-reversion result concerns the futures-spot basis, not price. The repo's own 1h shock fade, daily shock reversal and overnight-reversal tests were null, and the last one had the wrong sign (continuation).

The OI proxy is unreliable in exactly the target hours. On BTC 2021-05-19 (a cascade day) the 5m metrics rows for 11:30, 11:35 and 12:45 UTC are missing, so the 'row at or before' rule silently uses stale OI. Giagkiozis & Said find Binance BTC_USDT_P OI irreconcilable with volume over Jul-Sep 2023. Archive vintage is retroactive (2026-03 and 2026-07/08 re-uploads). The UM liquidation history that would validate the proxy does not exist (um/daily/liquidationSnapshot is empty).

The outcome is fat-tailed and dominated by a few famous cascades (2021-05-19, 2022-11, 2025-10-10) whose outcomes are known. The mean fade is driven by a few events, which lowers effective power further and raises snooping risk.
required_design_changes: (For any resubmission; closest to viable of the four, because it is perp-only and executable on the platform.) Set max OI staleness to 10 min. If either OI row is missing, drop the event and report the drop count. No silent fallback.

Make the primary claim the tradeable one: net fade return > 0 after taker fees and a stress-slippage assumption (for example, at least 2x the HMRV 5.95 bp stress spread). The OI-drop vs OI-rise contrast is a secondary requirement, not a substitute.

Delta-neutral arbitrageurs have the opposite incentive: they hold into T to collect funding. The sign is not determined a priori.

It cannot be confirmed with the proposed windows. My census of Binance realized funding (a proxy for fhat; the conditioning variable only, no returns read), using the SEAS-1 windows:

The size needed is far above anything documented. A 60-minute leg needs at least 10 bp net. With ~38 date clusters and 1h sigma ~0.5-0.8% (unverified), the MDE is ~20-27 bp gross. No published return evidence exists. Kim & Hansen 2026 find the quarter-hour pattern 'essentially unchanged when we exclude the three quarter-hours each day that coincide with funding settlement', at ~0.5 bp per boundary.

The T2 placebo is ambiguous and may leak look-ahead. If 'the identical rule applied at T-4h' means signing the window [T-5h, T-4h) with the fhat known at T-60m, the signal is used to sign an earlier return. fhat is built from the premium over [T-8h, T-60m), which tends to rise after price rises, so the placebo mean is biased and T2 is inflated toward a false positive.

The fhat estimator is mis-specified. For 8h intervals Binance uses a LINEARLY time-weighted average premium (weights 1, 2, ..., n), not an equal mean. The omitted last hour carries ~23% of the weight ((480^2 - 420^2)/480^2), so an equal mean over [T-8h, T-60m) is a biased proxy.

# Crypto research and execution stack: inventory (read-only, 2026-10-03)

**Summary.** Every crypto result in the repo is ICT or Wyckoff-family, built on Binance **spot** klines. Each one is negative, inconclusive, or shown to rest on a single trade. - **`scripts/risk_model.py`:**

## 6. Gaps that block a census-style crypto study

1. **Data length and type.**
   - Local 5m data is 1 year; 15m is 3 years; and all of it is spot.
   - Verified 2026-10-03 against the public endpoints:
     - USD-M perpetual REST klines start 2019-09-08 (BTC), 2019-11-27 (ETH) and 2020-09-14 (SOL) (`https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/klines?...&startTime=0`).
     - Spot BTCUSDT starts 2017-08-17 (`https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines?...&startTime=0`).
     - **The bulk archive starts 2020-01 for BTC and ETH, not 2019-09.** `https://data.binance.vision/data/futures/um/monthly/klines/BTCUSDT/5m/BTCUSDT-5m-2019-{09..12}.zip` returns 404 and `...-2020-01.zip` returns 200. The same pattern holds for `.../fundingRate/...`.
     - SOL archive files start 2020-09.
     - Funding REST history for BTC starts 2019-09-10 (`https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/fundingRate?symbol=BTCUSDT&startTime=1567900800000`).
   - No importer exists yet for perpetual klines, funding, mark price or premium index.
2. **Cost realism.**
   - Fees are an unverified VIP-0 assumption.
   - Slippage, spread, funding and basis are not modelled.
   - No crypto cost profile exists.
   - There is no continuous historical spread series. Archive `bookTicker` was present on 2023-06-01 and 2024-03-01, but returned 404 on 2021-06-01, 2022-01-01, 2024-06-01, 2025-06-01 and 2026-09-01.
   - Testnet fills cannot stand in for mainnet slippage (my inference, not verified).
3. **Funding schedule assumption is wrong for most alts.**
   - `https://fapi.binance.com/fapi/v1/fundingInfo` shows BTC, ETH, SOL and SUI fund **every 8h**.
   - ONDO, TAO, RENDER, VIRTUAL and ASTER fund **every 4h**, with cap/floor ±2%.
   - So "every 8h at 00/08/16 UTC" does not hold for 5 of the 9 symbols.
4. **24/7 day boundary.**
   - The census harness is built around the FTMO "server day" (broker rollover).
   - Its settings are FTMO-specific: `HIST_ROOT=data/history/ftmo`, `COST_PROFILE` is FTMO spread, `RC.server_zone(PROVIDER)` (`edge_census.py:37-40, 152-158`). Exits that cross the rollover are skipped. Detectors use cash-open/close tables per index.
   - Crypto needs a declared day (UTC 00:00 matches the engine's UTC date at `backtest-methods.py:2136`, the daily kline and a funding time), and a rule for whether weekends are included.
   - The same-minute placebo would mix weekend and weekday minutes unless stratified.
5. **Density rules.**
   - A "dense day" means at least 80% of the median bars per day, and at least 50 bars for a day to count as full (`edge_census.py:47, 103-107`). The rule was calibrated for CFD sessions.
   - A continuous market has about 288 5m bars per day, so outage holes (such as 2023-03-24) pass as dense. The quality gate flags any hole on a market that never closes.
   - The rule needs re-declaring, including how holes inside a window are handled.
6. **Data already viewed and statistical power.**
   - 2023-09 → 2026-09 on BTC/ETH/SOL is `development` and the last 6 months are EXPOSED. Data from 2026-09-13 onward is untouched, but that is only about 3 weeks.
   - Perpetual data before 2022-08 has never been read in the repo, but it is widely studied publicly.
   - The 9 symbols are highly correlated (the profile notes "near-perfectly correlated crypto"), so clustering standard errors by date matters even more.
7. **Risk definition.** Live sizing excludes fees and slippage from the 1% at-stop loss (`risk_model.py:135-159`), and the 0.75× notional cap changes realised risk for tight stops.

hypotheses.name: BTC post-US-close time-of-day premium (21:00-23:00 UTC long), with a DST test of the mechanism
hypotheses.mechanism: The literature puts BTC's positive drift in the hours after every major equity market has closed. The proposed explanation is liquidity and flow that is not tied to the equity session, plus inventory unwinding after the US close. A US-anchored effect has to move by one UTC hour when New York changes its clocks, and that gives a falsification test: since 2022, BTC's volatility peak follows New York DST and fades at the NYSE close. This is a pure time-of-day premium, which the repo has never measured because its same-minute placebo subtracts this kind of effect by construction (docs/plans/2026-10-03-reframes.md R6(a)).
hypotheses.rule: Instrument BTCUSDT USDT-M perp (primary); ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT as separate secondary tests counted in BH. Every calendar day d: buy at the open of the 1m bar starting 21:00:00 UTC and sell at the open of the 1m bar starting 23:00:00 UTC. Time exit only. A catastrophe stop at entry - 3 x ATR(1h, 24 bars), using only bars closed before 21:00 UTC, sets the size so a stop-out loses 1% of equity (owner's definition). The position is flat before 00:00 UTC, so there is no funding stamp. Primary statistic: mean net return per trade minus the mean of the same day's other 11 non-overlapping 2h windows. This is a seasonal null. Do NOT use the same-minute placebo, because it removes the effect being tested. Costs are pre-registered two ways: taker 0.05%/side (primary, risk-config) and maker 0.02%/side (secondary, assumes a fill at the touch). Pre-registered mechanism diagnostic, reported but not traded: compare the 2h window starting one hour after the NYSE close (20:00 UTC in US DST months, 21:00 UTC in standard-time months) with the fixed-UTC window. If the fixed-UTC window wins in both DST regimes, the 'post-US-close' story is false even if the premium is real. Reads: DISCOVERY / CONFIRMATION on 2020-01 to 2024-12 Binance perp data split 60/40. EXPOSED = 2025-01 to 2026-09. Note that the source's own sample ends 2022-02 and Quantpedia's update ends 2023-06.
hypotheses.holding: 2 hours, every day
hypotheses.expected_effect: Source gross: about 33%/yr annualized, vol 20.93%, MDD -22.45%, on Gemini BTCUSD hourly data from Oct-2015 to Feb-2022 (Padysak & Vojtko 2022, via Quantpedia). That is about 0.078% per trade gross (my arithmetic: ln(1.33)/365), which is BELOW the 0.10% taker round trip. Part of it is BTC's unconditional drift: about 65%/yr buy-and-hold x 2/24 is about 5%/yr, so the excess is about 0.065% per trade. Quantpedia's 2023 update reports 40.64% annualized over the whole sample to 2023-06, with a 'rough period' and a -22.7% MDD in 2022-23. Evidence after the ETF launch cuts against it: Schmidt & Kraft (SSRN 2026) report that hour of day predicts volume and volatility but NOT return direction (unverified: search snippet only, SSRN unreachable). Net expected effect at taker cost: about 0 or negative. At maker cost: about +0.02 to +0.04% per trade if the premium survived, which is unknown.

hypotheses.name: BTC 1-minute lead over allowlisted small/mid-cap alt perps (lagged catch-up after large BTC minute moves)
hypotheses.mechanism: Common shocks hit BTC first. Coins with less attention or liquidity adjust with a lag of about 1 minute because information spreads slowly across a fragmented market. A Binance 1-minute study finds that small caps correlate more with BTC at lag 1 than at lag 0, and a separate Binance study finds lagged returns of other coins predict focal coins out of sample after costs. The sign is contested: another study finds a NEGATIVE intraday lead from large to small coins (a 'seesaw' effect), so the test must be two-sided, with the positive sign pre-registered as primary.
hypotheses.rule: Universe: allowlisted alts SUIUSDT, TAOUSDT, RENDERUSDT, ONDOUSDT, VIRTUALUSDT, ASTERUSDT (test units). ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT are CONTROLS, expected to show no lag. Leader: BTCUSDT perp. At the close of each 1m bar t: event if |r_BTC,t| >= max(0.25%, 4 x sigma), where sigma = stdev of BTC 1m returns over the previous 1440 bars, excluding t. For each alt i, take beta_i from OLS of 1m alt returns on same-minute BTC returns over the previous 7 days (PIT). Gap g_i = beta_i x r_BTC,t - r_i,t. Enter alt i in direction sign(r_BTC,t) ONLY if sign(g_i) = sign(r_BTC,t) and |g_i| >= 0.10%. Entry price: the first aggTrade at least 2 seconds after bar t closes (latency haircut; do not use the idealized t+1 open). Exit: taker at the close of bar t+5. One position per alt; no new entry while one is open. Primary statistic: mean net return per trade vs a placebo of the same alt and same minute-of-day on non-event minutes. Pooled across alts with CR1 SE clustered by event minute. Sign test reported two-sided.
hypotheses.holding: About 5 minutes
hypotheses.expected_effect: UNKNOWN at a horizon tradable for this account. lit_cross_asset.json.notes:
I did not edit any repo files. The only files I wrote are scratch downloads under the scratchpad (xasset/). Five hypotheses, in prior order: XA2 > XA1 (cost-fragile) > XA3 (low power; refines the repo's untested candidate B4) > XA5 > XA4 (cost-fragile).

REJECTED candidates and why:
(1) CME weekend gaps. CME moved its crypto futures/options to 24/7 trading from 2026-05-29 (Yahoo/BeInCrypto 2026-06-01: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-first-cme-gap-free-174649486.html; CoinAlertNews: https://coinalertnews.com/news/2026/05/28/cme-24-7-crypto-futures-erases-bitcoin-gap, which mentions a weekly Sunday maintenance halt; the CME press pages were unreachable here). So the gap signal can no longer form live. The historical study I could read (Market Science, 2019-12-30, BitMEX, 105 gaps from 2017-12 to 2019-12: https://marketsscience.com/gap_study.html) found 95% eventual fills, but the fade-to-fill strategy had gross SR 0.20 (exit at Friday close) and -0.05. Fading over 24h/48h lost 0.49%/0.55% on average, i.e. the gap direction continued, but the author says it is 'not worth trading'. A weekend-continuation version on BTC itself is possible but has a weak prior and a structural break in 2026-05, so I did not pre-register it.
(2) Crypto-gold intraday link. I found no documented intraday return lead-lag. Baur & Hoang (JBEF 32, 2021: https://econpapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:beexfi:v:32:y:2021:i:c:s2214635021001052) find near-zero BTC-gold correlation across frequencies and quantiles. That makes gold useless as a signal source, but it is the basis for expecting near-zero correlation between the crypto books and the H7/G9 gold book.
(3) BTC overnight return predicting the next-day VIX change (Gu, Lin, Liu, SSRN 5186527, 2018-2023, coefficient -0.262, t -2.49, via https://aligrithm.com/bitcoins-overnight-returns-forecast-the-vix/). VIX is not in the allowlist, the significance is marginal, and the blog's own author distrusts it.
(4) Concretum's 'Monday Asia-open effect' (https://concretumgroup.com/seasonality-in-bitcoin-intraday-trend-trading/). Gross Sharpe for BTC intraday trend-following is about 1.6 over 2018-2025, with performance concentrated from Sunday 19:00 NY for about 24h and stronger after mid-2020. It is a candidate MODIFIER for any crypto intraday-trend family, not a standalone cross-asset signal. There are no costs and no hour-level table.

PROTOCOL notes:
- XA1 needs a seasonal null (other windows of the same day), not the repo's same-minute placebo, which subtracts the effect by construction (reframes R6(a)). The DST split is the mechanism test that separates 'US-close' from 'fixed-UTC'.
- XA3 is data source != venue (Binance signal, FTMO CFD execution). Its expected tradable effect is the residual AFTER the reopen. The published effects are mostly in the reopen gap, which a CFD trader entering after the reopen cannot capture.
- Natural EXPOSED windows are the post-publication periods: XA2 from 2024-11-12 and XA1 from 2023-07.
- Structural breaks to stratify on: LUNA (2022-05), US spot BTC ETFs (2024-01), CME 24/7 (2026-05-29).
- Data coverage checked via the data.binance.vision S3 listing on 2026-10-03: monthly 1m klines for BTC/ETH start 2020-01, not 2019-09 (daily or other intervals may start earlier; not checked). Funding files for BTCUSDT cover 2020-01 to 2026-09. Small-cap alt histories are short (ASTER about 13 months).

hypotheses.name: Perp-spot basis convergence (HMRV random-maturity arbitrage), delta-neutral
hypotheses.mechanism: Retail demand for leveraged longs, combined with scarce arbitrage capital, pushes the perp price away from its no-arbitrage value. Funding and arbitrage then pull it back at a random future time, so a hedged position that bets on convergence profits. HMRV find that most of the return comes from price convergence rather than funding: for BTC, 37.61 of 52.55 %/yr in their Table 8. Gornall-Rinaldi-Xiao find perp dislocations are small and short-lived even during stress.
hypotheses.rule: Universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and SOLUSDT, each as a Binance USDT-M perp plus Binance spot. At each 1h bar close t (UTC), compute prem_t = (F_t - S_t)/F_t from the 1h perp close F and 1h spot close S. Compute rho_t = 1095*prem_t + sgn(10.95% - r)*54.75% - r (HMRV eq. 17, with Binance kappa=1/8h, clamp gamma=0.05%/8h, interest iota=0.01%/8h, annualised x1095). r is a pre-registered constant of 5%/yr; 0% and 10% are reported as sensitivity only, because no PIT USDT borrow-rate series is in the archive. Round-trip cost of both legs: c = 2*(c_spot + c_perp). ENTRY at the next bar open: if rho_t > 1095*c, short the perp and buy equal notional of spot. If rho_t < -1095*c, go long the perp. The primary variant is long-spot-only, so this second leg is skipped; HMRV's long-only variant has BTC SR 8.20 at zero cost. EXIT both legs at the first bar close where rho crosses 0, which is HMRV's close threshold for every fee tier. Hard exits: a 30-day time stop, and a basis-blowout stop on adverse rho excursion, with notional sized so that loss at that stop = 1% of account. Funding is booked at each settlement while open. Placebo: the same holding-time distribution entered at random hours.
hypotheses.holding: Hours to days. HMRV high-fee tier: average open-to-close 96 h for BTC and 81 h for ETH.
hypotheses.expected_effect: HMRV Table 9, Binance 2020-01-08 to 2024-03-11, 'High' maker-fee tier (spot 0.0675%, perp 0.0144% one-way), net of fees plus effective spread: BTC SR 3.27, 12.55 %/yr return on notional, 3.84 % vol, MaxDD -2.63 %. ETH: SR 4.45, 18.18 %/yr. Their SRs are annualised over active hours only (BTC active 23 % of hours), which flatters them versus an always-invested Sharpe. At this repo's costs (perp taker 0.05% plus spot 0.10%, so c = 0.30%) the entry threshold is about 1.8x HMRV's high tier. No published result exists at that cost, so the effect at our costs is unknown.

EXIT when FR21 < 0.005%/8h, or when 3 consecutive realised funding prints are < 0, or after 90 days. Optional pre-registered second threshold (0.03%/8h); BH across the 2 thresholds x 3 symbols. Risk: an adverse basis move or a liquidation buffer on the short-perp leg, sized so that loss at that stop = 1% of account. Benchmarks: always-on carry over the same window (HMRV Table 7 'Carry' construction) and cash. In traditional futures, bases (leverage demand) negatively predict returns (Hazelkorn-Moskowitz-Vasudevan). In crypto, high carry is said to predict crashes (BIS). hypotheses.rule: Universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT perps. Decision daily at 00:00:05 UTC, using only data with timestamps <= 00:00 UTC. Member (a) FUNDING: FR21 = mean of the last 21 realised funding prints; P = its percentile rank within the trailing 365 daily values (365-day warm-up). LONG if FR21 < 0 and P <= 10. SHORT if P >= 90 and FR21 > 0.01%/8h. Member (b) OI: dOI7 = 7-day % change of sum_open_interest_value (last 5m row of the day, from metrics); SHORT if dOI7 percentile >= 90 and the 7-day price return > 0; LONG if dOI7 percentile >= 90 and the 7-day price return < 0. Execution: perp taker at 00:00:05 UTC; hold exactly 7 days; at most one open position per symbol per member, so signals arriving while a position is open are ignored. Stop: 3 x ATR(14, 1D) from entry, sized so that loss at stop = 1% of account; the effect test uses the raw 7-day return, and the stop applies only to trading P&L. hypotheses.name: Forced-deleveraging flush reversal: hourly shock with OI collapse (liquidation proxy) -> 6h fade
hypotheses.mechanism: A large hourly move during which open interest falls sharply suggests forced closures (liquidations, stop-outs) rather than new informed positioning. Forced, liquidity-driven flow should overshoot and partly revert. Crypto shows intraday reversal linked to overreaction, and its predictability patterns change around large jumps (Wen, Bouri, Xu, Zhao 2022). The test isolates the derivatives-flow part by contrasting OI-drop shocks with OI-rise shocks of the same size. This repo's 1h and daily shock fades on CFDs were null; this version differs in asset (crypto) and in the OI conditioning.
hypotheses.rule: Universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT perps, 1h bars UTC. At the close of hour h: r_h = ln(close/open); sigma = st.dev. of the prior 720 hourly returns (current hour excluded). OI_end = sum_open_interest (contracts) from the last 5m metrics row with create_time <= close(h) - 5 min. OI_start = the row at or before open(h). dOI_h = OI_end/OI_start - 1. EVENT: |r_h| >= 3*sigma AND dOI_h <= -1.5%. Both thresholds are frozen; a sensitivity cell of 4*sigma / -3% sits in the same BH family. TRADE: enter opposite to sign(r_h) at the open of h+1 (taker); exit at the close of h+6. Stop beyond hour h's extreme +0.5*sigma, sized so that loss at stop = 1% of account. Skip events within 6h of a previous event on the same symbol. CONTRAST (the pre-registered effect): the mean 6h fade return of OI-drop events minus that of control events with the same |r_h| >= 3*sigma but dOI_h >= 0. Same-hour-of-day placebo, CR1 clustered by date.
hypotheses.holding: 6 hours (fixed).
hypotheses.expected_effect: Unknown. No crypto study reporting returns after OI-identified deleveraging was found. Indirect support only: Wen et al. (2022, NAJEF; BTC Mar 2013 to May 2020) report both intraday momentum and reversal, with patterns that change around large price jumps. That is no number for this construction. Gornall-Rinaldi-Xiao document how the basis behaves in >5% hourly moves, not price reversal.

FINDINGS

hypotheses.name: H7 transfer to crypto: first 5m close beyond the prior UTC-day high/low, with 20-day momentum agreeing, held to the end of the UTC day
hypotheses.mechanism: Intraday trend continuation once price leaves yesterday's range in the direction of the medium-term trend. Late-informed or trend-chasing flow keeps pushing, and short-dated stops and liquidations sit just beyond the prior-day extremes. This is the same mechanism as gold H7, the repo's only robust CFD edge. Crypto-specific literature splits by horizon. Breakouts of short ranges REVERSE at horizons of 3 hours or less (Corbet et al. 2019; Kitron & Wengrowicz 2026). At about 12-24h they turn to positive but insignificant continuation (Corbet et al. 2019, 1440-min row). Within days that are already abnormal, prices continue to the close (Caporale & Plastun 2020, not point-in-time). A hold to the end of the UTC day sits right at that crossover, so it is a genuine transfer test, not a sure thing.
hypotheses.rule: Copy the H7 definition from /Users/tungnguyen/TYME/Trading/trading-decision-system/docs/plans/2026-10-02-edge-f3-preregistration.md and change only 'server day' to 'UTC day [00:00,24:00)'. No crypto-specific tuning. Universe: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT USDT-M perps, using Binance MAINNET archive prices. Inputs are frozen at 00:00 UTC of day D from completed bars only. PDH/PDL = max high / min low of the 288 5m bars of D-1. MOM20 = sign(ln(close of D-1 / close of D-21)), using daily closes at 00:00 UTC. Signal: if MOM20>0, the first 5m bar of D whose CLOSE > PDH triggers a long. If MOM20<0, the first 5m CLOSE < PDL triggers a short. Closes beyond the non-aligned boundary are ignored. At most one trade per symbol per day, and no trade when MOM20=0. Entry: taker at the open of the next 5m bar. Exit: taker at the 23:55 UTC bar close, so the position is flat before the 00:00 funding stamp. The measured rule has no stop, the same as the gold census. Funding: apply the realized fundingRate at the 08:00/16:00 stamps if the position is open. Measurement uses the repo protocol. Excess = net trade return minus the placebo. The placebo is the same symbol, same entry 5m slot, same exit and same weekday, taking the unconditional return signed by trade direction. Use CR1 by UTC date and BH q=0.10 across the family. Also report raw net returns, because a same-minute placebo hides clock premia. Reads, each done once: DEVELOPMENT = 2020-01-01 to 2024-02-29 (SOL from 2020-10-01). DISCOVERY = first 60% of development days, CONFIRMATION = last 40%, EXPOSED = 2024-03-01 to latest archive month. Optional pre-perp read: Binance SPOT 2017-08 to 2019-12 with perp fees and no funding, declared before any run. A stop for sizing under the owner's 1%-at-stop rule (e.g. the opposite prior-day boundary) is a separate forward-stage parameter. It must be re-measured, not assumed.

This is NOT point-in-time (days selected on their final return, sigma estimated in-sample), so treat it as an upper bound only. Gold H7 in this repo: annual Sharpe ~0.86 (from the task context).

hypotheses.name: G9 transfer to crypto: volatility breakout from the UTC open (open +/- 0.5 x prior-day range), held to the end of the UTC day
hypotheses.mechanism: Williams/Crabel volatility breakout. A move from the open larger than half of yesterday's range signals order imbalance that continues for the rest of the day. On crypto perps, liquidation and stop flow amplifies it, because forced orders are price-insensitive. This is the same mechanism as gold G9, which survived in this repo, with silver on watch. It has no trend filter, so it differs from H7: it fires on counter-trend expansion days too.
hypotheses.rule: Copy the G9 definition from /Users/tungnguyen/TYME/Trading/trading-decision-system/docs/plans/2026-10-02-edge-f4-preregistration.md and change 'server day' to 'UTC day'. k=0.5 is unchanged. Every crypto day counts as dense. Inputs for day D: O_D = open of the 00:00 UTC 5m bar, R = PDH - PDL of the 288 5m bars of D-1. Upper = O_D + 0.5R, Lower = O_D - 0.5R. Signal: the first 5m bar of D whose CLOSE > Upper triggers a long, and the first whose CLOSE < Lower triggers a short. Only the first event counts, one trade per symbol per day. Entry: taker at the next 5m open. Exit: taker at the 23:55 UTC bar close, before the 00:00 funding stamp. The measured rule has no stop. Funding at 08:00/16:00 is applied if the position is open. Placebo, CR1, BH family, read windows and the optional spot pre-perp read are identical to CRY-H7, and both count in ONE family. Pre-register two diagnostics that sit outside the BH family: a weekday/weekend split, and a split by whether D-1 was an NR4 day (range compression). hypotheses.name: Reversal after large NEGATIVE hourly shocks on crypto perps (long-only, 24h and 6h holds), with an open-interest-drop (liquidation proxy) variant
hypotheses.mechanism: Overreaction and liquidity-provision premium. Large hourly down-moves in crypto are partly driven by price-insensitive forced selling (liquidations, stops), which creates temporary price pressure. Liquidity providers who buy demand a premium that grows with volatility and crash risk. Evidence is asymmetric: overreaction appears after NEGATIVE shocks and is largest 6-24h after the event (Miralles-Quiros & Miralles-Quiros 2022). Intraday reversal is described as 'unique to crypto' in Wen et al. 2022. This is the opposite sign to CRY-H7/G9, so the family adjudicates continuation against reversal after large moves.
hypotheses.rule: Use UTC-aligned 1h bars of the perp. sigma_h(t) = SD of the 720 hourly log returns ending at bar t-1, excluding bar t. A shock occurs at bar t if r_t <= -3 x sigma_h(t). Entry: long at the first 1m open after bar t closes. Exit: at the close of bar t+24 (primary test) or bar t+6 (secondary test). Both holds are in the family. No new entry is allowed while a position on that symbol is open, which prevents overlap during crash clusters. OI variant (a separate test): additionally require dlnOI over bar t to be <= the 5th percentile of the trailing 720 hourly dlnOI values. OI comes from the sum_open_interest field of the data.binance.vision daily 'metrics' files (5-min snapshots), using the snapshot stamped at least 5 min before bar t's close. Control (positive shock >= +3 sigma, short, 24h) is reported as a diagnostic outside the BH family. Funding is charged at the realized rate at each 00/08/16 UTC stamp crossed. Measurement: excess over a placebo with the same symbol, same entry hour-of-week and same hold, taking the unconditional long return. Use CR1 by UTC date, which is essential because shocks cluster. Same reads as CRY-H7. Family: 3 symbols x {neg-24h, neg-6h, neg+OI-24h} = 9 tests.
hypotheses.holding: 24 hours (primary) and 6 hours (secondary).
hypotheses.expected_effect: Magnitude is UNVERIFIED. The publisher full text (Taylor & Francis) was blocked, so only the abstract is verified: 'clear evidence of overreaction after negative shocks ... especially important between 6 and 24 hours after the event'. A search snippet reported filter sizes of +/-0.5% to +/-5% on hourly returns; I did not open the page that states this, so treat it as unverified. The sample period is also unverified. Wen et al. (2022): both intraday momentum and reversal exist in BTC/ETH/LTC/XRP, 2013-03 to 2020-05, and patterns change around large jumps. Counter-evidence: Caporale & Plastun (2019, JES) find counter-movement trading after DAILY overreactions not profitable. This repo's 1-hour shock fade on CFDs (symmetric, 1-2h hold) differs in asset, sign asymmetry and hold.

hypotheses.name: Multi-day Donchian-channel breakout ensemble (long-only, vol-targeted) on BTC/ETH/SOL perps, the crypto analog of 'first close beyond the range with trend'
hypotheses.mechanism: Time-series momentum and trend-following. In crypto, trend chasing by retail traders who use leverage and scarce arbitrage capital produce persistent multi-day trends (Liu & Tsyvinski 2021; BIS Crypto carry 2023). The intraday literature above suggests crypto continuation shows up at horizons of a day or more rather than within the day. This is therefore the best-documented crypto breakout construction, and a hedge in case CRY-H7/G9 fail intraday. It overlaps with any trend/TSMOM sweep, so de-duplicate.
hypotheses.rule: Pre-register the published specification without tuning. The rule details below come from SECONDARY summaries; the primary is on SSRN, which was not reachable. Lookbacks L in {5,10,20,30,60,90,150,250,360} days, using daily closes at 00:00 UTC. For each L: enter long at the next daily open when close_D > max(close over the prior L days). The trailing stop = max(previous stop, midpoint of the L-day close channel). Exit at the next open when close_D < stop. Position = (active sub-signals / 9) x (25% / annualized 90-day realized vol), capped at 1.0x equity notional. Rebalance only if the target deviates by more than 20% from the current position. Long-only. Costs: taker 0.05% per side on traded notional, plus realized funding at every 8h stamp on held notional. Use Binance SPOT daily closes from 2017-08 only to warm up the 360-day channels, so signals exist from 2020-01. Measurement: daily net return of the strategy minus a vol-matched always-long null (same 25% target and cap, same costs and funding). This tests timing value, not crypto beta. Use HAC/CR1 by date. Also report alpha vs BTC. Reads: the repo split, PLUS a pre-registered POST-PUBLICATION read from 2025-05-06 (SSRN posting) to latest, because the paper's sample covers the whole development window.
hypotheses.holding: Days to months per sub-signal, with daily evaluation.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Primary abstract: a rotational top-20 coin portfolio achieved net-of-fees Sharpe above 1.5 and annualized alpha of 10.8% vs BTC, on a survivorship-free dataset of coins traded since 2015. Secondary third-party summaries of the paper's Table 3, unverified against the primary: BTC from Jan-2015 CAGR 30%, vol 17%, Sharpe 1.56, MaxDD 19%; ETH from Aug-2015 Sharpe 1.51; net of 10 bp fees, spot execution, so no funding. Counter-evidence: Hudson & Urquhart (~15,000 technical rules) find significant in-sample predictability, but none for Bitcoin out-of-sample.

MAIN READ ACROSS THE LITERATURE
Crypto short horizons (3h or less) are mean-reverting and too thin to trade:
- Corbet et al. 2019: TRB breakouts of 180 min or less reverse significantly on BTC 1-min data, 2014-2018.
- Kitron & Wengrowicz 2026 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888): 15-min reversal in 90% of 183 Binance pairs since 2021, about 1.3 bp gross vs 5 bp cost.
- JRFM 2026 (https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.3390/jrfm19090692): BTC rules on 12h sessions fail the SPA test and the 2021-2025 holdout.
- Shen, Urquhart, Wang 2022 (https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/100181/3/21Sep2021Bitcoin%20Intraday%20Time-Series%20Momentum.R2.pdf): BTC first half-hour predicts the last half-hour (slope 0.968, NW t 4.38, R2 1.44%; data to 2020-12), but break-even costs are only 3/7/10 bp, below the 10 bp taker round trip. The paper's claim that leverage raises break-even cost is wrong, because fees scale with notional.

Continuation appears only at about 12-24h (Corbet's 1440-min row, positive but insignificant) and at multi-day horizons (Donchian/TSMOM). So moving gold's intraday continuation to crypto is plausible only with a hold to the end of the day, and the prior is weaker than for gold.

Recommended order:
1. CRY-H7 and CRY-G9 as one family. They are a direct transfer with no tuning.
2. CRY-NSR. It is the opposite sign, so the family tests continuation against reversal.
3. CRY-DON. It has the strongest crypto evidence, but high contamination and a heavy funding drag.

CONSIDERED AND NOT PROPOSED
- Noise-area intraday momentum (Zarattini, Aziz, Barbon, 'Beat the Market', SPY 2007-2024; https://alexandria.unisg.ch/bitstreams/a99aba00-f967-49b3-aceb-f544dc386e0b/download): unlevered 9.7%/yr over 7,668 trades is about 2 bp per trade (my arithmetic). That dies at 10 bp crypto taker and is fragile on CFD index spreads. Related index constructions (Gao, ORB, G9) are already null in this repo.
- NR-type compression: I found no peer-reviewed crypto evidence, only news and practitioner claims, and the repo's NR7 on CFDs is null. It is kept only as a diagnostic split inside CRY-G9.
- Deribit option-expiry reversal (Weiss et al. 2026, FRL 110340; https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1016/j.frl.2026.110340): reversal around the 08:00 UTC expiry, concentrated on high ATM open-interest and negative-gamma days. The magnitude is unverified (ScienceDirect 403), and OI/gamma data are not in the Binance archive. It is a candidate for a later microstructure sweep, using last-Friday expiries as a calendar proxy.
- Caporale & Plastun next-day overreaction trades: their own 2019 paper finds them not exploitable.

PLACEBO WARNING
Crypto has documented clock premia:
- Turn-of-candle at minutes 0/15/30/45 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10015199/).
- A quarter-hour effect on Binance perps where opening order imbalance predicts 4-12h returns (Kim & Hansen 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09426; the 2021-01 to 2024-10 sample comes from a search snippet and is unverified).
- A Monday-Asia-open effect (Concretum).
Keep the same-minute placebo, add weekday matching, and also report raw net returns, since the placebo hides time-of-day premia.

hypotheses.name: Crypto post-US-close 2-hour window long (21:00-23:00 UTC), with a New-York-anchored mechanism variant
hypotheses.mechanism: Published hour-of-day premium. Bitcoin's highest hourly returns fall in the hours ending 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, the period after all major equity markets have closed (Padysak and Vojtko 2022; Quantpedia 2022 and 2023). The source labels each hour by its closing time, so 'return at 22:00' is 21:00-22:00. The proposed explanation (the window is free of traditional-market hours) is the authors' conjecture. Two other explanations are possible but unverified: the CME daily maintenance break and the timing of the US cash close. If the effect is tied to US hours, a DST-aware New York window should be sharper than the fixed UTC window. Variant B tests exactly that.
hypotheses.rule:
Family SEAS-1, pre-registered before any read. It has 6 tests: {A: UTC-fixed, B: NY-anchored} x {BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT}, all Binance USDT-M perps.

Variant A: every calendar day, 7 days a week, go long with a taker order at the open of the 1h kline whose openTime is 21:00 UTC. Exit with a taker order at the open of the 23:00 UTC kline.

Variant B: the window is 17:00-19:00 America/New_York, DST-aware (21:00-23:00 UTC under EDT, 22:00-24:00 UTC under EST). When the window end coincides with an actual fundingTime from the fundingRate file, exit at the open of the 1m bar one minute earlier, so no funding is exchanged.

No Friday or high-volatility filters. Quantpedia found those after the fact, so they are excluded.

Sizing for the owner's 1%-at-stop rule: stop = entry x (1 - 3*sigma2h). sigma2h is the standard deviation of all non-overlapping 2h log returns over the trailing 30 UTC days ending before entry. Notional = 1% of equity / (3*sigma2h). The stop is checked on 1m lows and is gap-aware (fill at the 1m open if the bar gaps through the stop).

Tests per read:
- T1: mean net log return per trade > 0, one-sided. Cost 0.05% per side taker; funding is 0 by construction.
- T2 (seasonal null): e_d = r_window,d - (2/24) x r_day,d > 0. r_day is the 24h close-to-close return of the day containing the window (UTC day for A, NY day for B). This measures excess over the instrument's own uniform drift.

A test survives a read only if T1 and T2 both pass. BH q=0.10 is applied over the 6 tests on discovery. CR1 standard errors are clustered by date.

Reported descriptively but not tested: the window's rank among all 24 two-hour start hours.

Windows for BTC: use post-publication data only. Development runs 2022-03-01 to 2025-09-30 (60/40 split); exposed runs 2025-10-01 to latest. ETH and SOL use the same windows; both are out-of-source in any period.
hypotheses.holding: 2 hours, time exit. Never holds through a funding timestamp.
hypotheses.expected_effect:
Source (Padysak & Vojtko 2022 via Quantpedia; Gemini BTC spot, 2015-10-09 to 2022-02-03, no costs): 33% per year, volatility 20.93%, max drawdown -22.45%. Quantpedia update to 2023-06-30: 40.64% per year, Calmar 1.79, max drawdown -22.7%.

Derived by me from those figures (gross, in-sample):
- About +7.8 bp per trade, from ln(1.33)/365.
- Per-trade sigma about 1.10%, from 20.93%/sqrt(365).
- About 800 trades are needed for t=2 on the gross effect, which is about 2.2 years per symbol.

No net, post-2023 or ETH/SOL effect has been published.

hypotheses.name: Funding-timestamp pre-settlement pressure and post-settlement rebound, conditional on a PIT funding estimate
hypotheses.mechanism: Funding is exchanged only by positions open at the funding timestamp. When the PIT-estimated rate is extreme, the paying side has an incentive to close just before T and reopen after it. That would mean selling pressure into T when funding is positive (and buying when negative), then a rebound after T. What is documented is only that volatility and volume spike at Binance's funding hours, 00h and 16h, less at 08h (Hansen, Kim, Kimbrough 2021). Evidence against a large effect at the 15-minute scale: Kim & Hansen (2026) find their quarter-hour return predictability 'essentially unchanged' when the funding quarter-hours are excluded. The prior is weak, so this is exploratory.
hypotheses.rule:
Family SEAS-3, 6 tests: {PRE, POST} x {BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT}.

For every actual fundingTime T in the symbol's fundingRate file (not assumed to be 00/08/16, because Binance can move contracts to 4h schedules):
1. At T-60m, compute fhat = Pbar + clamp(i - Pbar, -0.05%, +0.05%). Pbar is the mean of 1m premiumIndexKlines closes over [T - interval, T-60m); i = 0.01% x interval/8h.
2. If fhat >= +0.03% (3x baseline):
   - PRE: short with a taker order at the open of the 1m bar at T-60m; cover at the open of the 1m bar at T-1m. No funding is exchanged.
   - POST: long at the open of the 1m bar at T+1m; exit at T+61m.
3. If fhat <= -0.01%: the mirror image (PRE long, POST short).

The thresholds are fixed a priori and not tuned. Sizing uses the 1%-at-stop rule with stop = 3 x trailing-30-day 1h sigma.

Tests per read:
- T1: net > 0.
- T2 (clock and sentiment placebo): mean(signed return in the leg) - mean(signed return of the identical rule applied at T-4h, a non-settlement clock hour on 8h schedules, same fhat condition) > 0.

T2 separates the settlement effect from funding simply predicting returns. BH q=0.10 over the 6 tests; CR1 standard errors clustered by date.
hypotheses.holding: 60 minutes per leg
hypotheses.expected_effect: Unknown. I found no published estimate of returns around funding timestamps. He, Manela, Ross & von Wachter do not study intraday behaviour at funding times. Context only: Kim & Hansen 2026 put the sign-weighted quarter-hour forecast at about 0.5 bp per boundary, about one tenth of one taker fee.

hypotheses.name: Negative crypto weekend predicts weak US index Monday: short US500/USTEC CFDs (asymmetric)
hypotheses.mechanism: Crypto trades through the weekend while equities are closed, so weekend crypto returns carry risk-sentiment information. Mourey, Shahrour & Soiman (2025) find that negative weekend crypto returns predict Monday equity declines, while positive weekend returns do not (loss aversion). Family SEAS-4, 4 tests: {entry A, entry B} x {US500, USTEC}.

For each Monday that is a US cash trading day, define W = ln(BTCUSDT perp price at the entry time / BTCUSDT perp close at the preceding Friday 16:00 America/New_York), both from Binance 1m bars. Primary condition: W < 0 (only negative weekends trade).
- Entry A: short at the first FTMO 1m bar at or after Monday 09:30 ET (US cash open); exit at Monday 15:55 ET.
- Entry B: short at the first FTMO 1m bar after the CFD weekend reopen, with W computed to that bar; exit at Monday 15:55 ET. Swap is charged if applicable.

Use the repo's FTMO server-time convention (us_dst_dates_fixed_offset). Sizing: the 1%-at-stop rule with stop = entry + 3 x trailing-60-Monday sigma of the same window.

Tests per read:
- T1: net > 0 after repo real_costs.
- T2 (calendar null): mean(short return | W<0) - mean(short return | all Mondays, same window, same read) > 0. This is the excess over the instrument's own Monday drift.
